content:
We need a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: step1 forward: carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). So retrosynthesis: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and amine.

Step2: Doebner modification: forward forms α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. So retrosynthesis: break C=C double bond and carboxylic acid to give aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually Doebner gives unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. So reverse: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid (or malonic acid decarboxylated). So we can split the unsaturated acid fragment (C= C - C(=O)N) maybe the unsaturated acid part is /C=C/C(=O)N... Actually target has /C=C/C(=O)N... So the unsaturated acid is the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). The forward Doebner would produce that unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid. So retrosynthesis: break the C=C and C=O to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). However the amide is formed later, so maybe step1 is amide formation from carboxylic acid (the unsaturated acid) and aniline. So step2 is Doebner to get unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. Step3 is sulfonamide formation: forward sulfonyl chloride + amine gives sulfonamide. In target, sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings: NS(=O)(=O) attached to first ring (with methyl) and second aromatic ring (with unsaturated amide). So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid?) and aniline. Likely sulfonyl chloride + amine. So reverse: target -> sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) and aniline (Ar-NH2). The aniline is the first aromatic ring with methyl (para? Actually Cc1ccc(N... )cc1). So we can propose that.

Thus three steps:

1. Break amide: product -> unsaturated acid (α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline. So retrosynthesis: unsaturated acid + aniline.

2. Break unsaturated acid via Doebner: unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) + malonic acid.

3. Break sulfonamide: sulfonamide -> sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) + aniline (the methyl phenyl amine). The sulfonyl chloride is attached to second aromatic ring (the one with aldehyde). So we get sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) and aniline (methyl phenyl amine).

Thus final precursors: methyl aniline (p-toluidine) (C c1ccc(N)cc1), sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) where Ar is the aromatic ring bearing aldehyde (c2ccc(Cl?) Actually after step2 we have aldehyde ring, which after sulfonyl chloride formation would be Ar-SO2-Cl? Wait sulfonyl chloride is attached to aromatic ring that later becomes sulfonamide linking to first ring. So the sulfonyl chloride is the second aromatic ring (the one with aldehyde). So its SMILES: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2? But also later after Doebner we will have aldehyde on that ring, so the sulfonyl chloride must be on that ring before aldehyde? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the aromatic ring that later also gets the unsaturated acid via Doebner? The target has sulfonamide attached to second aromatic ring which also has the unsaturated amide substituent. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same aromatic ring bearing a sulfonyl chloride group and later after Doebner we will attach the unsaturated acid to that ring? Wait the unsaturated acid is attached to the same aromatic ring via the amide (C(=O)N...). The sulfonamide attaches the nitrogen of the first ring to the sulfonyl group attached to the second ring. So the second ring has both sulfonyl group (SO2) attached to it and also the unsaturated amide substituent attached to the sulfonyl nitrogen? Actually the structure: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the sulfonyl group which is attached to the second aromatic ring. The unsaturated amide is attached to the second aromatic ring as a substituent (para to sulfonyl?). So the second ring has two substituents: sulfonyl attached to N of first ring, and the unsaturated amide attached via carbon chain.

Thus retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride attached to second ring and aniline (first ring). Then break amide to give unsaturated acid attached to second ring and aniline (third ring). Then break unsaturated acid via Doebner to give aldehyde attached to second ring and malonic acid.

Thus final precursors: p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1), sulfonyl chloride aromatic (c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2), aldehyde aromatic (c2ccc(CHO)cc2)?? Wait the same aromatic ring cannot be both sulfonyl chloride and aldehyde simultaneously; but after sulfonyl chloride step, the aromatic ring already has sulfonyl chloride; after Doebner step, the aldehyde is on that same ring? Actually Doebner uses aromatic aldehyde as starting material, not sulfonyl chloride. So perhaps the order is different: first Doebner to create unsaturated acid on aromatic aldehyde, then sulfonamide formation attaches the first aromatic amine to the sulfonyl group on the second ring (which already has the unsaturated amide). So sulfonyl chloride precursor is the aromatic ring bearing the unsaturated acid (already formed) and a sulfonyl chloride group. So step2: Doebner gives unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring (no sulfonyl). Step3: sulfonyl chloride addition to that ring? Actually sulfonyl chloride is attached to aromatic ring via S(=O)2Cl substituent; the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the aromatic ring, not the unsaturated acid. So we need a precursor where the aromatic ring has both sulfonyl chloride and aldehyde? That seems unlikely.

Alternative: The sulfonyl chloride precursor is the aromatic ring with sulfonyl chloride, and then after sulfonamide formation we have sulfonamide attached to first ring, then later we do Doebner on that same aromatic ring (which already has sulfonamide) to attach unsaturated amide. So order: 1) sulfonamide formation (break sulfonamide) -> sulfonyl chloride + aniline. 2) amide formation (break amide) -> unsaturated acid + aniline (the third ring). 3) Doebner (break unsaturated acid) -> aldehyde + malonic acid.

Thus three steps as required.

Now we need to produce JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each step. We have some template IDs from search results: For sulfonamide formation, template ID 733 (reaction_id) with retro_smarts_template showing sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride and aniline. So we can use template_id "733". For amide formation, need template where carboxylic acid + amine -> amide. Search for that.
